title: Correlation between the dynamic change in the pubis–sling distance and the change in IPSS after TVT surgery – a pilot study (SPINDLE → Sling–Pubis Interaction and Dynamic Link Evaluation)
summary:
The tension-free vaginal tape (TVT) procedure is a well-established treatment for stress urinary incontinence, meaning involuntary urine leakage during coughing, sneezing, or physical exertion. Although the procedure is very successful in most cases, some patients report difficulties with urination after surgery. Depending on the study and the length of follow-up, such symptoms occur in approximately 2% to 14% of operated women.

One possible reason for these symptoms is changes in the position and shape of the implanted sling after surgery. These include, for example, changes in the distance and angle between the sling and the pubic bone, as well as changes in the angle and mobility between the bladder and the urethra, particularly during straining (Valsalva maneuver). Such changes may influence urination and lead to symptoms.

In this study, it will be investigated prospectively, meaning over time, whether there is an association between the position of the sling, measured by ultrasound at rest and during straining, and subjectively perceived urinary symptoms. For this purpose, various ultrasound measurements (distances, angles, and sling shape) will be compared with changes in the IPSS questionnaire, which assesses the severity of symptoms.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Women aged 18–80 years with a planned retropubic TVT procedure
Preoperative post-void residual urine ≤ 100 mL
Ability to provide informed consent
Participation in routine postoperative follow-up
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria:
Clinically relevant postoperative post-void residual urine (> 100 mL)
Need for sling loosening or re-operation
Neurological disorders affecting micturition
Pregnancy
Lack of informed consent
History of sling surgery or major urethral surgery
Current treatment with unstable anticholinergic or β3-agonist medication
